v: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham became the father of Isaac. Isaac became the father of Jacob. Jacob became the father of Judah and his brothers.
Judah became the father of Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez became the father of Hezron. Hezron became the father of Ram.
Ram became the father of Amminadab. Amminadab became the father of Nahshon. Nahshon became the father of Salmon.
Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab. Boaz became the father of Obed by Ruth. Obed became the father of Jesse.
Jesse became the father of King David. David became the father of Solomon by her who had been Uriah’s wife.
Solomon became the father of Rehoboam. Rehoboam became the father of Abijah. Abijah became the father of Asa.
Asa became the father of Jehoshaphat. Jehoshaphat became the father of Joram. Joram became the father of Uzziah.
Uzziah became the father of Jotham. Jotham became the father of Ahaz. Ahaz became the father of Hezekiah.
Hezekiah became the father of Manasseh. Manasseh became the father of Amon. Amon became the father of Josiah.
Josiah became the father of Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the exile to Babylon.
After the exile to Babylon, Jechoniah became the father of Shealtiel. Shealtiel became the father of Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel became the father of Abiud. Abiud became the father of Eliakim. Eliakim became the father of Azor.
Azor became the father of Zadok. Zadok became the father of Achim. Achim became the father of Eliud.
Eliud became the father of Eleazar. Eleazar became the father of Matthan. Matthan became the father of Jacob.
Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations; from David to the exile to Babylon fourteen generations; and from the carrying away to Babylon to the Christ, fourteen generations.
b: This passage records the genealogy of Jesus Christ: fourteen generations from Abraham to David, fourteen from David to the exile in Babylon, and fourteen from the exile to the Christ. The list highlights Jesus as the son of David and the offspring of Abraham. It reminds us that His coming is the fulfillment of a promise, and that God keeps what He has pledged to His people.

Through this passage God shows us His faithfulness and His power to fulfill His promises. Many generations passed, yet God never let go of His plan, and at the appointed time He brought the Redeemer, Jesus Christ, into the world. His faithfulness does not change, and His grace and promises will surely be fulfilled in our lives too.

This passage calls us to trust God's promises. Whatever difficulty or challenge we face right now, God's love and plan never change. We can receive this truth in faith and believe that God will lead us through every season of life.
q: How do I view God's faithfulness and His power to fulfill His promises?
Do I have faith that God will lead me through times of difficulty and challenge?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was like this: After his mother, Mary, was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found pregnant by the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, being a righteous man, and not willing to make her a public example, intended to put her away secretly.

But when he thought about these things, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take to yourself Mary, your wife, for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Spirit.
She shall give birth to a son. You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins.”
Now all this has happened that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying,
“Behold, the virgin shall be with child, and shall give birth to a son. They shall call his name Immanuel;” which is, being interpreted, “God with us.”
Joseph arose from his sleep, and did as the angel of the Lord commanded him, and took his wife to himself;
and didn’t know her sexually until she had given birth to her firstborn son. He named him Jesus.
b: This passage tells of the birth of Jesus Christ. Mary was engaged to Joseph, but before they came together she was found to be with child by the Holy Spirit. Joseph, a righteous man, did not want to disgrace her publicly, so he planned to divorce her quietly. But as he considered this, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream and told him not to be afraid to take Mary as his wife, for the child in her was from the Holy Spirit. The son would be named Jesus, because He would save His people from their sins. All this fulfilled what the prophet had spoken: a virgin would conceive and bear a son, and they would call His name Immanuel, which means "God with us."

In this passage God shows us two important things. The first is His grace and wonderful plan: Jesus Christ was born of the virgin Mary to be the Savior of mankind. This shows God's love and kindness, setting us free from the bondage of sin and giving us eternal salvation. The second is God's guidance and protection: Joseph obeyed God's will because of the message in his dream, took Mary as his wife, and became Jesus' earthly father. This reminds us to rely on the Holy Spirit's leading in daily life and to submit to God's will.
q: Am I willing to submit to God's will as Joseph did?
When I face difficulties, can I trust God's guidance and protection?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of King Herod, behold, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem, saying,
“Where is he who is born King of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east, and have come to worship him.”
When King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
Gathering together all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he asked them where the Christ would be born.
They said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for this is written through the prophet,
‘You Bethlehem, land of Judah, are in no way least among the princes of Judah: for out of you shall come a governor, who shall shepherd my people, Israel.’ ”
Then Herod secretly called the wise men, and learned from them exactly what time the star appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem, and said, “Go and search diligently for the young child. When you have found him, bring me word, so that I also may come and worship him.”
They, having heard the king, went their way; and behold, the star, which they saw in the east, went before them, until it came and stood over where the young child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
They came into the house and saw the young child with Mary, his mother, and they fell down and worshiped him. Opening their treasures, they offered to him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country another way.
b: This passage tells the story of Jesus' birth. In the days of King Herod, wise men from the east came to Jerusalem looking for the child born "King of the Jews." They said they had seen His star in the east, a sign of His birth, and had come to worship Him. But the news troubled King Herod and all of Jerusalem with him.

Herod carefully questioned the chief priests and scribes, who told him that according to the prophets the King would be born in Bethlehem of Judea. Herod secretly called the wise men and learned from them exactly when the star had appeared. Then he sent them to Bethlehem and told them to search carefully for the child. After they set out, the star went ahead of them until it stopped over the place where the child was. When they saw the star, they rejoiced greatly, entered the house, and bowed before Jesus and Mary. They opened their treasures and offered Him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
Then, warned in a dream not to return to Herod, the wise men went back to their own country by another way.
This passage shows that the birth of Jesus stirred up political and religious unrest. It also shows that Jesus' coming brings great hope: He is the Savior of the world and its King.

In this passage God shows us His presence and guidance. Just as the star led the wise men to Jesus, God will guide us in our lives. He gives clear direction when we seek His will and submit to His leading. We can trust His guidance at every stage of life, and He will lead us on the right path.
Let us thank the Holy Spirit for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.
q: How do you respond to God's guidance and direction?
Are you willing to submit to God's will and pursue His plan and purpose for your life?

v: Now when they had departed, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Arise and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt, and stay there until I tell you, for Herod will seek the young child to destroy him.”
He arose and took the young child and his mother by night, and departed into Egypt,
and was there until the death of Herod; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Lord through the prophet, saying, “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

Then Herod, when he saw that he was mocked by the wise men, was exceedingly angry, and sent out, and killed all the male children who were in Bethlehem and in all the surrounding countryside, from two years old and under, according to the exact time which he had learned from the wise men.
Then that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled, saying,
“A voice was heard in Ramah, lamentation, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; she wouldn’t be comforted, because they are no more.”
b: This passage describes King Herod's plot to kill Jesus. God appeared to Joseph in a dream and told him to take the child and Mary and flee to Egypt, because Herod was going to search for the child and destroy Him. Joseph obeyed, took his family to Egypt, and stayed there until God told them to return.

This passage shows us God's protection and guidance. He not only protected Jesus from Herod's persecution but also fulfilled what the prophet had spoken: "Out of Egypt I called my son." It reminds us that God's plans and grace are always exact and always fulfilled.

Through this passage God shows us His protection and guidance. He cares not only for our spiritual life but also for our bodies and our safety. When we face difficulty and danger, we can trust God and rely on His guidance and protection. No one can obstruct God's plan; He will surely accomplish His purpose.
q: Have you experienced God's protection and guidance in your life?
How do you respond to such grace?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: But when Herod was dead, behold, an angel of the Lord appeared in a dream to Joseph in Egypt, saying,
“Arise and take the young child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who sought the young child’s life are dead.”
He arose and took the young child and his mother, and came into the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in the place of his father, Herod, he was afraid to go there. Being warned in a dream, he withdrew into the region of Galilee,
and came and lived in a city called Nazareth; that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophets that he will be called a Nazarene.
b: This passage tells how, after Herod died, an angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt and told him to take the child and His mother back to the land of Israel, for those who sought the child's life were dead. Joseph obeyed and brought Jesus and His mother back to Israel. But when he heard that Archelaus had succeeded his father Herod as king, he was afraid to go there. Warned again in a dream, he went to the region of Galilee. So Joseph settled with Jesus and His mother in a city called Nazareth, fulfilling what the prophets had said, that Jesus would be called a Nazarene.

This passage reminds us that God's plan is perfect and faithful. By speaking to Joseph through an angel in dreams, God protected the life of Jesus. It also shows that God's promises and leading are true and reliable at every stage of our lives.

God is saying to me that He is our protector and guide. Just as He protected Jesus, He will protect us and lead us along the path He has prepared for us. We can trust His plan and His promises, even in times of difficulty and uncertainty, because His love and grace are with us always.

Let us meditate on this: Do we believe in God's protection and leading? Are we willing to trust His plan even when we face difficulty and uncertainty? Let us seek God's guidance in our daily lives and walk in faith on the path He has prepared for us.
q: Do you believe in God's protection and leading?
In what areas of life do you need to trust God's plan more?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: In those days, John the Baptizer came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea, saying,
“Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!”
For this is he who was spoken of by Isaiah the prophet, saying, “The voice of one crying in the wilderness, make the way of the Lord ready! Make his paths straight!”
Now John himself wore clothing made of camel’s hair, with a leather belt around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
Then people from Jerusalem, all of Judea, and all the region around the Jordan went out to him.
They were baptized by him in the Jordan, confessing their sins.
But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for his baptism, he said to them, “You offspring of vipers, who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?
Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance!
Don’t think to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham for our father,’ for I tell you that God is able to raise up children to Abraham from these stones.
“Even now the ax lies at the root of the trees. Therefore every tree that doesn’t produce good fruit is cut down, and cast into the fire.
I indeed baptize you in water for repentance, but he who comes after me is mightier than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his threshing floor. He will gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn up with unquenchable fire.”
b: This passage tells of John the Baptist preaching in the wilderness of Judea, calling people to repent because the kingdom of heaven was at hand. He quoted the prophet Isaiah: a voice crying in the wilderness, "Prepare the way of the Lord; make His paths straight." John was a striking figure, dressed in camel's hair with a leather belt around his waist, eating locusts and wild honey. Many people from Jerusalem and Judea went out to him, confessing their sins and being baptized by him in the Jordan River. But when John saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming to be baptized, he warned them not to merely flee from wrath, but to bear fruit worthy of repentance.

This passage shows us that God, through John the Baptist, delivered an important message: the kingdom of heaven is at hand, and we should repent. This is God's call to us to turn to Him, leave the path of sin, and openly confess our sins before Him. God does not care only about outward change; He wants us to bear fruit worthy of repentance, showing a true change of heart and a living faith.
q: Have I truly repented?
Is there fruit in my life that shows repentance?
In what areas do I need to work harder at changing my thoughts and behavior?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him.
But John would have hindered him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?”
But Jesus, answering, said to him, “Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he allowed him.
Jesus, when he was baptized, went up directly from the water: and behold, the heavens were opened to him. He saw the Spirit of God descending as a dove, and coming on him.
Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.”
b: "Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan to John, to be baptized by him. But John would have hindered Him, saying, 'I need to be baptized by you, and you come to me?' But Jesus, answering, said to him, 'Allow it now, for this is the fitting way for us to fulfill all righteousness.' Then he allowed Him. Jesus, when He had been baptized, went up directly from the water: and behold, the heavens were opened to Him. He saw the Spirit of God descending like a dove, and coming on Him. Behold, a voice out of the heavens said, 'This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased.'"

This passage tells how Jesus came to the Jordan and chose to be baptized by John. John at first was unwilling, because he knew Jesus was sinless and he baptized only sinners. But Jesus persuaded him, saying it was right to fulfill all that God had appointed. After Jesus was baptized, the heavens opened, and the Spirit of God descended like a dove and rested on Him. At the same time a voice came from heaven: "This is my beloved Son, with whom I am well pleased."

Through this passage God shows us several important truths. First, Jesus was baptized to be our example, showing humility and obedience. Though He was sinless, He humbly accepted John's baptism, showing us the heart of a servant.

Second, the passage reminds us that the Spirit of God is the presence and anointing of Jesus. When Jesus was baptized, the Spirit came upon Him, a sign of God's authority and power revealed to the world. It also reminds us that when we are baptized and become Christians, God's Spirit is upon us as well, giving us strength and guidance.

Finally, the voice from heaven declared Jesus to be God's beloved Son, with whom He is well pleased. This was God's announcement to the world of Jesus' identity and mission, and a testimony to His obedience and sinlessness. In the same way, as God's children we can live each day a life that pleases God, by listening to His word and submitting to His will.
q: Are you willing to be humble and obedient like Jesus, and accept God's will?
In your life, can you understand God's voice and live in a way that pleases Him?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Then Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
When he had fasted forty days and forty nights, he was hungry afterward.
The tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.”
But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God’s mouth.’ ”
Then the devil took him into the holy city. He set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down, for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you,’ and, ‘On their hands they will bear you up, so that you don’t dash your foot against a stone.’ ”
Jesus said to him, “Again, it is written, ‘You shall not test the Lord, your God.’ ”
Again, the devil took him to an exceedingly high mountain, and showed him all the kingdoms of the world, and their glory.
He said to him, “I will give you all of these things, if you will fall down and worship me.”
Then Jesus said to him, “Get behind me, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and you shall serve him only.’ ”
Then the devil left him, and behold, angels came and served him.
b: This passage tells how Jesus was led by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil. Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights, and He was hungry. The devil took the opportunity to come and tempt Him. First he suggested that Jesus turn stones into bread, but Jesus answered with Scripture: man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of the mouth of God. Then the devil took Jesus to the pinnacle of the temple in the holy city and urged Him to throw Himself down, to prove by a spectacular miracle that He was the Son of God. Again Jesus answered with Scripture and refused to put the Lord His God to the test. Finally the devil took Jesus to a very high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory, offering them to Jesus if He would bow down and worship him. Jesus firmly refused the devil's temptation and held fast that only the Lord God is to be worshiped and served. Then the devil left Him, and angels came and ministered to Him.

This passage tells us that Jesus endured the devil's temptations in the wilderness, yet He stayed faithful to God throughout. By answering with Scripture, He showed that He trusted the guidance and truth of the Bible and wanted only to do God's will. It reminds us that when we are in temptation, we too can rely on God's word and truth to resist the devil. God has given us the Bible as the standard and guide for our lives, and we need to keep learning it, meditating on it, and obeying its teaching, letting the Holy Spirit's leading and God's word direct our lives.

Through this passage God says to me that, whatever the time and whatever the temptation, we should remain faithful to the Lord our God and resist the devil's attacks. We can rely on the guidance and truth of the Bible and believe that God's word has the power to protect and guide us. At the same time, we should always seek to worship and serve the Lord our God, and not be deceived by the temptations of the world.
q: When I face temptation, do I rely on God's truth and word to resist the devil's attacks?
Do I remain faithful to the Lord my God, seeking to worship and serve Him rather than being led astray by the temptations of the world?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Now when Jesus heard that John was delivered up, he withdrew into Galilee.
Leaving Nazareth, he came and lived in Capernaum, which is by the sea, in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali,
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying,
“The land of Zebulun and the land of Naphtali, toward the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles,
the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, to those who sat in the region and shadow of death, to them light has dawned.”
From that time, Jesus began to preach, and to say, “Repent! For the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand.”
Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”
They immediately left their nets and followed him.
Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.
They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed him.
Jesus went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the Good News of the Kingdom, and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

The report about him went out into all Syria. They brought to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and torments, possessed with demons, epileptics, and paralytics; and he healed them.
Great multitudes from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and from beyond the Jordan followed him.
b: This passage tells how, after John was put in prison, Jesus withdrew into Galilee. He left Nazareth and went to live in Capernaum, which was by the sea, in the borders of Zebulun and Naphtali. This fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah: Galilee of the Gentiles, the people who sat in darkness saw a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death, light had dawned. From that time Jesus began to preach, proclaiming that the kingdom of heaven was at hand and calling people to repent.

As He walked beside the Sea of Galilee, Jesus saw Peter and Andrew, brothers who were fishermen. He said to them, "Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of men." They immediately left their nets and followed Him. Likewise Jesus saw James and John, the sons of Zebedee, in a boat mending their nets. He called them, and they immediately left the boat and their father and followed Him.

Jesus taught in the synagogues throughout Galilee, proclaimed the gospel of the kingdom, and healed people of every kind of disease. His fame spread throughout Syria, and people from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and beyond the Jordan followed Him.

This passage tells us that Jesus called disciples and began His ministry, proclaiming the gospel of the kingdom, healing the sick, and doing signs and wonders. Through these things God shows us His mission and purpose: He came to save the world and to bring light and redemption.

What this passage reveals to me is that Jesus invites us to follow in His footsteps, to lay down the entanglements of the world and follow Him wholeheartedly. We should also follow Jesus' example in ministry, proclaiming the gospel, healing the hurting, and showing forth the glory of God.
q: Am I willing to lay down my comforts and the entanglements of the world, follow Jesus wholeheartedly, proclaim the gospel, and show God's love?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Seeing the multitudes, he went up onto the mountain. When he had sat down, his disciples came to him.
He opened his mouth and taught them, saying,
“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled.
Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God.
Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness’ sake, for theirs is the Kingdom of Heaven.
“Blessed are you when people reproach you, persecute you, and say all kinds of evil against you falsely, for my sake.
Rejoice, and be exceedingly glad, for great is your reward in heaven. For that is how they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
b: This passage tells how Jesus, seeing the multitudes, went up on the mountain and sat down, and His disciples came to Him. He began to teach them and spoke the Beatitudes.

First, Jesus said, "Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." This tells us that if we keep a humble and poor-in-spirit attitude, we can enter into the grace of the kingdom of heaven.
Next, Jesus said, "Blessed are those who mourn, for they shall be comforted." This reminds us that in sorrow and difficulty, God will comfort us and give us strength and peace.

Jesus went on, "Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth." Gentleness is a virtue. When we treat others with a gentle heart, we not only win people's respect, but also receive God's favor and gifts.

Jesus continued, "Blessed are those who hunger and thirst after righteousness, for they shall be filled." This tells us that when our longing for righteousness and truth surpasses everything else, God will give us spiritual fullness and satisfaction.

Then Jesus said, "Blessed are the merciful, for they shall obtain mercy." This reminds us to be full of compassion and love toward others, because when we show mercy, God will also bless us with mercy.

Jesus went on, "Blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God." This reminds us to keep a pure heart, to clear away every evil thought and impurity, so that we can draw closer to God and enjoy His presence.

Next Jesus said, "Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called children of God." This teaches us to work for harmony and peace, because God commends those who make peace and calls them His children.

Finally, Jesus said, "Blessed are those who have been persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven." This reminds us that in trials and persecution we can rejoice because of heaven's blessing, and God will give us an even greater reward.
This passage shows us God's heart for us. We are to live according to God's heart and become blessed people.
q: How do I show humility, mercy, and a hunger for righteousness in my life?
Do I have opportunities to work for reconciliation and peace?
In hardship and adversity, how do I keep my joy and faith?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “You are the salt of the earth, but if the salt has lost its flavor, with what will it be salted? It is then good for nothing, but to be cast out and trodden under the feet of men.
You are the light of the world. A city located on a hill can’t be hidden.
Neither do you light a lamp, and put it under a measuring basket, but on a stand; and it shines to all who are in the house.
Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
“Don’t think that I came to destroy the law or the prophets. I didn’t come to destroy, but to fulfill.
For most certainly, I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not even one smallest letter or one tiny pen stroke shall in any way pass away from the law, until all things are accomplished.

Whoever, therefore, shall break one of these least commandments, and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.
For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, there is no way you will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven.
b: This passage is mainly about the mission and influence of believers in the world. Jesus told His disciples that they are the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Salt is a seasoning, and if it loses its flavor it is good for nothing, except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot. In the same way, if we as believers lose our connection with Christ and His spiritual grace, we lose our influence on the world. Light stands for our good works and the testimony of our lives, which can brighten the lives of others. Jesus calls us to let our light shine, so that people may see our good works and glorify our Father in heaven.

Through Jesus' words, this passage shows us two important truths. First, as Christians we must stay connected to Christ and keep seeking and following God's will, so that we can be the salt of the earth and the light of the world. Second, the influence of our conduct and lives on others is very important. We should let good works reflect God's love and goodness, so that people can see the glory of Christ in us.
q: Do my words and actions in daily life reflect the glory of Christ?
How can I be salt and light in the world, so that people see God's love and goodness?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “You have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not murder;’ and ‘Whoever murders will be in danger of the judgment.’

But I tell you that everyone who is angry with his brother without a cause   will be in danger of the judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca!’  will be in danger of the council. Whoever says, ‘You fool!’ will be in danger of the fire of Gehenna.
“If therefore you are offering your gift at the altar, and there remember that your brother has anything against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Agree with your adversary quickly, while you are with him on the way; lest perhaps the prosecutor deliver you to the judge, and the judge deliver you to the officer, and you be cast into prison.
Most certainly I tell you, you shall by no means get out of there, until you have paid the last penny.
b: This passage records Jesus teaching about relationships between brothers and sisters and the importance of reconciliation. Jesus quoted the commandment in the law of Moses, "You shall not murder," and went further: we must not kill in deed, nor harbor anger in our hearts or hurt others with harsh words. Jesus tells us that anger or insults directed at a brother or sister will be subject to judgment and consequences.

Through this passage God explains two important truths to me. First, God values our relationships with others, especially with our brothers and sisters. They are people God loves, and we should treat them with love and respect. Second, God calls us to deal promptly with conflict and quarrels. If, while we are worshiping God, we remember that someone has something against us, we should go and be reconciled with them at once, so that our relationship with God is not hindered.
q: Have I been reconciled with my brothers and sisters?
Do I hold anger or thoughts that hurt others? Let me examine my life and make sure I handle my relationships well, building a harmonious fellowship on love and peace.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand these truths and to walk in them. May God bless you.

v: “You have heard that it was said,  ‘You shall not commit adultery;’
but I tell you that everyone who gazes at a woman to lust after her has committed adultery with her already in his heart.

If your right eye causes you to stumble, pluck it out and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.

If your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off, and throw it away from you. For it is more profitable for you that one of your members should perish, than for your whole body to be cast into Gehenna.
“It was also said, ‘Whoever shall put away his wife, let him give her a writing of divorce,’
but I tell you that whoever puts away his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, makes her an adulteress; and whoever marries her when she is put away commits adultery.
b: This passage records Jesus' teaching on marriage and adultery. Jesus first quoted the commandment "You shall not commit adultery," and then explained that it is not only the act: even lustful thoughts in the heart are already sin. Jesus tells us to keep our hearts pure and not let impure thoughts enter.

Jesus went on to say that if our right eye or right hand causes us to stumble, we should tear it out or cut it off and throw it away; it is better to lose one part of the body than for the whole body to be cast into sin. This is Jesus' most serious call to act decisively when facing temptation: to stay pure and keep far from sin, we must make sacrifices and firm decisions.

Finally, Jesus spoke about divorce. He quoted the Mosaic provision about giving a certificate of divorce, but added that except for sexual immorality, divorcing a wife makes her an adulteress. Here Jesus stresses the sanctity of marriage and the importance of lifelong faithfulness. We should keep faithful love toward our spouse and not dissolve the marriage covenant lightly.

Through this passage God tells us what He expects of us regarding marriage and purity. He wants us to keep our thoughts pure and stay away from sexual immorality and evil thoughts. He also calls us to hold to the sanctity of marriage and not abandon the marriage covenant lightly.
q: Am I pure in my thoughts and actions? Am I faithful to my partner?
How can I be more watchful in guarding my thoughts?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Again you have heard that it was said to the ancient ones, ‘You shall not make false vows, but shall perform to the Lord your vows,’
but I tell you, don’t swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Neither shall you swear by your head, for you can’t make one hair white or black.
But let your ‘Yes’ be ‘Yes’ and your ‘No’ be ‘No.’ Whatever is more than these is of the evil one.
b: This passage records Jesus' teaching on oaths and honesty. According to what was said to the people of old, they were warned not to break an oath, and the oaths they swore had to be kept. But here Jesus tells His disciples not to swear at all, because we cannot control heaven, the earth, Jerusalem, or even a single hair on our own head. Instead, Jesus calls His disciples to speak plainly and sincerely, and to be people of their word: let your "Yes" be "Yes," and your "No," "No."

This passage brings us a word from God. God wants us to be honest, truthful, and trustworthy people, who do not need oaths to make us keep our promises. God cares about the attitude of our hearts and the truthfulness of our speech. He hopes that when we deal with others, we express ourselves with honesty and integrity, and do not let oaths become a tool to cover up or hide our true intentions.
q: In our daily lives, do our promises and oaths to others match our actions?
Do we deal with others sincerely and truthfully? In this area, how can we become more like Jesus Christ?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye, and a tooth for a tooth.’
But I tell you, don’t resist him who is evil; but whoever strikes you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also.
If anyone sues you to take away your coat, let him have your cloak also.
Whoever compels you to go one mile, go with him two.
Give to him who asks you, and don’t turn away him who desires to borrow from you.
“You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor  and hate your enemy.’
But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
that you may be children of your Father who is in heaven. For he makes his sun to rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
If you only greet your friends, what more do you do than others? Don’t even the tax collectors do the same?
Therefore you shall be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
b: This passage records Jesus' teaching on how to treat enemies and evildoers. He told His disciples not to resist with revenge but to respond with love. If someone strikes you on the right cheek, turn the other to him also; if someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well; if someone forces you to go one mile, go with him two. Jesus also said to love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven.

What is God telling us through this passage? First, He wants us to live out the life of God's children. He wants us to love one another with His life, not only loving those who love us, but loving our enemies and evildoers too. This is a challenge, because human nature tends toward an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth, but God calls us to rise above that instinctive response and to treat others with love by God's life. Furthermore, Jesus teaches us not to seek revenge but to be willing to become servants of others, even putting our own interests second. This is how a true Christian lives out the life of Christ.

Through this passage, God gives us an important revelation: the power of love and kindness is greater than hatred and revenge. When we treat others with love, we can be children of our Father in heaven and show forth His image and glory. Jesus set the example Himself, willing to die for us and for our sins, the greatest demonstration of love.
q: When facing enemies and evildoers, can we hold to Jesus' teaching and respond with love?
Are we willing to pray for them and treat them with kindness and forgiveness?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Be careful that you don’t do your charitable giving before men, to be seen by them, or else you have no reward from your Father who is in heaven.

Therefore when you do merciful deeds, don’t sound a trumpet before yourself, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, that they may get glory from men. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
But when you do merciful deeds, don’t let your left hand know what your right hand does,
so that your merciful deeds may be in secret, then your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
b: This passage records Jesus' teaching on giving to the needy. Jesus told His disciples not to do their giving deliberately before others in order to win their praise and glory. Instead, He encouraged them to give humbly and in secret, so that only the Father knows the good they do. Jesus said that when we do good in secret, the Father sees it and will reward us.

God is saying to me that He pays attention not only to our actions but even more to the motives of our hearts. God wants our giving to come from love and care, not from a desire to be seen by others or to win their approval. He encourages us to do good humbly and to give all the glory to Him alone.

This passage reminds us to examine our attitudes and motives. We can ask ourselves: When I do good, is it out of real love and care, or to win others' praise and admiration? Am I willing to do good in secret, only for God's glory? This lets us reflect on whether there are selfish motives in our lives, and to reorient the purpose of our good deeds.
q: What is my motive for doing good?
Am I willing to give the glory to God rather than seek human approval?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for caring about the motives of our hearts, and for wanting our good deeds to come from true love and care rather than from our own glory. Help me stay humble and hidden, doing good only for Your glory. Let all that I do be a testimony that honors You, and may Your will be fulfilled in my life. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.
In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.
Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.
b: This passage records Jesus' teaching on prayer. Jesus tells us that when we pray, we should not be like the hypocrites who deliberately stand in public places or on street corners to pray, just so that people will see their devotion. Instead, we should go into our private room and speak with our Father who is in secret. Our Father who sees in secret will surely answer our prayer.

Jesus also warns us not to use many repetitive words as the Gentiles do. They think that the more words they use, the more likely they are to be heard. But Jesus points out that our Father already knows what we need, and we do not need extra words to persuade Him. We should pray with a sincere and earnest heart, knowing that our Father is ready to answer our prayers.

What this passage shows us is that prayer is a way to build an intimate relationship with God. We are urged to meet with God in private and to pray with a sincere and restrained heart. Our Father already knows our needs, so we can confidently entrust everything to Him and believe that He will take care of us.
q: In prayer, do I sincerely communicate with God, or do I perform for others to see?
Do I believe God already knows our needs, and am I willing to entrust everything to Him?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us the true meaning of prayer. May we come to You in private with sincere and restrained hearts. Help us believe that You already know what we need, so that we can lay down our worries and confidently entrust everything to You. May Your will be done in our lives. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us today our daily bread.
Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.
Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’
“For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.
But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
b: This passage records the pattern Jesus gave His disciples for how to pray, known as the Lord's Prayer. This prayer has five parts, and each part holds important truths and petitions.
First, we are taught to hallow God's name. This reminds us to treat God with reverence and respect, and to regard His name as utterly holy.
Second, we ask for God's kingdom to come and His will to be done on earth as it is in heaven. This means we should seek God's kingdom and His will, and follow the example of Christ's life.
Next, we ask for our daily bread. This part reminds us to trust God to supply the needs of our lives, and to learn to be thankful and content with what He provides.

Then, we ask God to forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors. This teaches us to learn to forgive others, and to understand the grace and love of God, who sent Christ to pay the price for us.

Finally, we ask God to lead us not into temptation and to deliver us from evil. This reminds us to rely on God's great power, and to seek His protection and help to overcome the temptations and trials of sin.

This passage helps us understand that prayer is not only telling God our needs and wishes, but also a way of expressing our reverence and submission to Him. Through this passage God reminds us that our attitude should be one of humility, gratitude, and peace with others, and that we need to depend on God's guidance and protection.
q: In our prayers, are we truly seeking God's kingdom and His will?
Is there resentment or unforgiveness I need to let go of?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, we thank You for Your teaching, which helps us understand the important truths of prayer. May we honor Your name with reverence before You. May Your kingdom come and Your will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Provide for us our daily bread, and let us be thankful. Forgive us our debts, and help us learn to forgive others. Lead us away from temptation and evil, and let us rely on Your great power to overcome all things. In the name of Jesus Christ I pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;
so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.
b: This passage records Jesus' teaching on fasting. Jesus points out that when we fast, we should not be like the hypocrites, who deliberately put on a gloomy face so that others can see they are fasting. They do it only so that people notice their devotion, not out of a sincere seeking of God's grace. Jesus stresses that the purpose of fasting is not to attract attention but to build a deeper relationship with God.

Jesus tells us that when we fast, we should anoint our head and wash our face, so that no one can tell we are fasting. This reminds us that before God, fasting is a hidden act, seen only by our Father in secret. God sees the intentions and motives of our hearts in secret, and He will surely reward us, giving us the grace and blessing we need.

This passage tells us that fasting is not only an outward act; what matters more is the attitude of the heart. We should seek sincere communion with God, and not fast to show off our devotion. Fasting is a spiritual discipline that helps us focus more on God's will and draw closer to Him in private.

Through this passage God tells us that fasting is not merely a religious ritual; more importantly it is spiritual training and a deeper connection with God. When we fast with a sincere heart, God will surely see and answer our prayers. This passage reminds us that what matters is not outward appearance but the motives and attitudes of our hearts.
q: Is fasting a real spiritual experience for me?
When I fast, am I focused on connecting with God, or on having others notice my devotion? Let us examine our attitudes and motives, and seek a true meeting with God.
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us in Scripture the importance of sincere fasting. May our fasting not be to display our own devotion, but to build a deeper relationship with You. Help us come to You with sincere hearts, seeking Your grace and blessing in secret. May our fasting bring us more opportunities to draw near to You, and may our souls be renewed and cleansed. In the name of the Lord Jesus I pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;
for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
b: This passage teaches about wealth. Jesus tells us not to set our hearts on treasures on earth, because earthly treasures can be destroyed and stolen. Instead, Jesus encourages us to set our hearts on treasures in heaven, because treasures there are eternal and cannot be destroyed or stolen. Jesus also reminds us that where our treasure is, there our heart will be also.

This passage helps us see that we should not view wealth with worldly eyes, but treat it with eternal values. God is saying to me that wealth cannot truly bring happiness and satisfaction, because it is temporary and easily passes away. What truly matters is our pursuit of treasure in heaven, which transcends time and material things and can bring real abundance and joy.
q: Are my thoughts and pursuits focused mainly on earthly treasures, or on the eternal values of heaven?
Am I willing to give my life and wealth fully to God and seek treasure in heaven?
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!
“No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.
b: This passage speaks of the eye as the lamp of the body. If our eye is clear, that is, if our heart is full of God's true light, then our whole body will be full of light. But if our eye is bad, that is, if our heart has no room for the true word of God, then our whole body will be full of darkness. This passage reminds us that what our eyes fix upon, and the thoughts and intentions of our hearts, have a great influence on our lives.

In this passage God shows me two important truths. First, God wants our hearts to be filled with His true light, so that our lives can shine with light and hope. We need to let God's word and truth illuminate our hearts, so that we can see the world, other people and ourselves rightly. Second, God reminds us that we cannot serve two masters, meaning God and wealth. We must not turn away from God's will in pursuit of material satisfaction, because that only brings more darkness and loss.

Through this passage God reveals an important truth to us: we need to keep a longing and seeking for God in our hearts, and let His word and truth guide our lives. We must not let the pursuit of material things blind us to our love for God and our devotion to Him. Only when we put God first, and listen to His word and teaching, can we light up this dark world and become His witnesses.
q: How do I keep a longing for God in my heart?
Is there anything in my life, any possession or pursuit, that hinders my devotion to God?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us in this passage to keep our hearts full of Your true light, so that our lives may shine with light and hope. Help us to let Your word and truth illuminate our hearts, so that we see the world, others and ourselves rightly. Guide us also not to be disturbed by the temptations of material things, so that we always put You first, listen to Your word and teaching, and become witnesses who shine in this dark world. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?
“Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?
Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,
yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?
“Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.
But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.
Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.
b: This passage teaches us not to worry about the basic needs of life, such as food, drink and clothing. Jesus reminds us that life is more than food, and the body more than clothing. He points to the birds of the sky and the flowers of the field: they do not toil, yet God cares for them and clothes them with care. Jesus goes on to ask whether we can add a single hour to our life, or a single cubit to our height, by worrying. The answer is no. So why worry about clothing? If God cares for flowers and birds that are worth less than we are, He will certainly not forget us, whom He has created and loves.

Through this passage God shows us that we need not worry about the basic needs of life, because we have a loving heavenly Father who knows what we need. We should seek first God's kingdom and His righteousness, and all these things will be added to us. We should trust in God's provision, lay down our anxiety, and focus on pursuing His will and His kingdom.

Let us reflect on our own life: Are we often anxious about material needs and outside pressures? Do we believe that God loves us and will provide everything we need? Let us seek God's kingdom, put Him at the center of our lives, entrust our worries to Him, and trust His provision and guidance.
q: How can I show confidence in God's provision in my life?
Do I often entrust my worries to God and seek His kingdom and His will?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us not to worry about the basic needs of life, for You will provide all that we need. Help us to lay down our anxiety, seek Your kingdom, and trust Your provision and guidance. May our lives be focused on pursuing Your will and Your kingdom. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.
For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.
Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?
Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?
You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
“Don’t give that which is holy to the dogs, neither throw your pearls before the pigs, lest perhaps they trample them under their feet, and turn and tear you to pieces.
b: This passage records an important principle in Jesus' teaching: do not judge others, and do not use our own standards to evaluate them. Jesus tells us that when we judge others, we will be judged ourselves. He then expresses this principle in a parable: first take the plank out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother's eye.

Through this passage God shows us the importance of tolerance, understanding and love. We must not judge others with a self-centered attitude, but look at their faults with kindness and tolerance. At the same time, we need to examine our own imperfection and sin, and humbly receive God's forgiveness.

In our daily lives, we can reflect on whether we often judge others, and whether we evaluate their actions or choices too much from our own point of view. We can think about how to treat others with more tolerance and kindness, and seek strength from God to remove the sins and flaws in our own lives.
q: How do I view the faults of others?
When I evaluate others, do I use the love and tolerance of Jesus Christ as my standard? I need to examine my own attitude and conduct, and ask God to help me remove my own sin and flaws.
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for teaching us not to judge others or to evaluate them by our own standards. Help us to look at others with tolerance, kindness and love, while humbly examining ourselves and receiving Your grace and forgiveness. May we remove the plank from our own eye, and see clearly in order to help others. In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Ask, and it will be given you. Seek, and you will find. Knock, and it will be opened for you.
For everyone who asks receives. He who seeks finds. To him who knocks it will be opened.
Or who is there among you, who, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks for a fish, who will give him a serpent?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
Therefore whatever you desire for men to do to you, you shall also do to them; for this is the law and the prophets.
“Enter in by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and many are those who enter in by it.
How narrow is the gate, and restricted is the way that leads to life! Few are those who find it.
b: This passage records Jesus teaching His disciples on the mountain how to ask, seek and knock, and reminding them that God is a Father who is glad to answer their prayers and seeking. Jesus uses the picture of fathers who are willing to give good things to their children; how much more will our Father in heaven give good things to those who ask Him.

Through this passage God shows us several important truths. First, He encourages us to ask, seek and knock with all our heart, trusting that He will hear and answer our prayers. Second, He reminds us to treat others with the same love and generosity with which He treats us. Finally, He tells us that the gate leading to life is narrow, and that those who find the way are few compared with those on the road to destruction. This reminds us to hold fast to our faith in daily life, to do what is right, and to choose and follow the teaching of Jesus Christ.
q: In your life, do you truly love the Lord, and do you treat others with the same love?
How do you put these truths into practice in your daily life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your abundant love and mercy to us through Your word. Give us firm faith, that we may ask, seek and knock with all our heart, trusting that You will answer our prayers. May we follow Your love and generosity and treat others with the same kindness. Help us to choose the way of Jesus Christ and hold fast to our faith, so that we may receive eternal life. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravening wolves.
By their fruits you will know them. Do you gather grapes from thorns, or figs from thistles?
Even so, every good tree produces good fruit; but the corrupt tree produces evil fruit.
A good tree can’t produce evil fruit, neither can a corrupt tree produce good fruit.
Every tree that doesn’t grow good fruit is cut down, and thrown into the fire.
Therefore by their fruits you will know them.
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter into the Kingdom of Heaven; but he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven.
Many will tell me in that day, ‘Lord, Lord, didn’t we prophesy in your name, in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
Then I will tell them, ‘I never knew you. Depart from me, you who work iniquity.’
b: This passage warns us to be on guard against false prophets and hypocritical behavior. False prophets may look like sheep on the outside, but inside they are wolves, and the fruit they bear shows their true nature. A good tree bears good fruit, and a bad tree bears bad fruit; this is a basic rule. Not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only those who do the will of the Father. Even if some boast that they have done things in the Lord's name, performed miracles and preached the gospel, if their conduct departs from God's will, Jesus will plainly tell them that He never knew them.

This passage reminds us to be careful in discerning people's true motives and actions. We should look not only at a person's appearance and words, but even more at their fruit, that is, the results that their conduct and life produce. We should take God's will as our guide and strive to walk in His way, not merely speaking the Lord's name but putting it into action. Only then can we truly draw near to the Lord and enter the kingdom of heaven.

Let us reflect on our own life: Are we truly doing God's will? Does our conduct match the example of a Christian? Let us examine our own fruit, and consider whether our actions truly reflect our relationship with God.
q: Do we focus only on outward appearances and neglect the true condition of the heart?
Do our actions and fruit match the faith we profess?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us to be on guard against false prophets and hypocrisy. Give us wisdom to discern the heart, so that we are not deceived by appearances but judge by the fruit of people's lives. Help us to do Your will, not merely speaking Your name but showing Your glory through our actions. May we walk with You at all times and enter Your kingdom. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: “Everyone therefore who hears these words of mine, and does them, I will liken him to a wise man, who built his house on a rock.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it didn’t fall, for it was founded on the rock.
Everyone who hears these words of mine, and doesn’t do them will be like a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
The rain came down, the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat on that house; and it fell—and great was its fall.”
b: This passage tells us that those who hear the words of the Lord Jesus and put them into practice are like a wise man who builds his life on a solid foundation, the rock. This foundation represents faith in God and obedience to His word. When they face all kinds of difficulties and trials, their faith does not waver, and their lives do not collapse. But if we only hear the words of the Lord Jesus and do not obey them, we are like a foolish man who builds his life on sand, with no solid foundation. When the storm comes, our lives will be badly damaged or even collapse completely.
This passage reminds us that God wants us not merely to hear the word but to do it. We need to unite faith with action and build on God's truth. Only then can our lives be settled and secure.

Through this passage God tells us that we must not stop at listening to messages and studying God's word; what matters more is putting God's word into practice in our lives. God wants us to build on His truth and love, so that we are not only blessed ourselves but can stand firm in difficulties and tests and become a witness to others.
q: Am I someone who both hears the word and does it?
Do I join my faith with my actions and build on God's truth?
What concrete steps can I take to make my life more solid and stable?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for reminding us that hearing and doing the word are equally important. May we join faith with action and build on Your truth and love, so that our lives stand firm. Give us wisdom and strength to stand unshaken in trials and become witnesses of Your love. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: When he came down from the mountain, great multitudes followed him.
Behold, a leper came to him and worshiped him, saying, “Lord, if you want to, you can make me clean.”
Jesus stretched out his hand, and touched him, saying, “I want to. Be made clean.” Immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
Jesus said to him, “See that you tell nobody, but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
When he came into Capernaum, a centurion came to him, asking him,
and saying, “Lord, my servant lies in the house paralyzed, grievously tormented.”
Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
The centurion answered, “Lord, I’m not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and my servant will be healed.
For I am also a man under authority, having under myself soldiers. I tell this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and tell another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and tell my servant, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard it, he marveled, and said to those who followed, “Most certainly I tell you, I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel.
I tell you that many will come from the east and the west, and will sit down with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the Kingdom of Heaven,
but the children of the Kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.”
Jesus said to the centurion, “Go your way. Let it be done for you as you have believed.” His servant was healed in that hour.
b: This passage tells how Jesus came down from the mountain and many people followed Him. A man with leprosy came to Him and said with full confidence that if the Lord was willing, He could make him clean. Moved by his faith, Jesus reached out His hand and touched him, and immediately he was made clean. Then a centurion came and asked Jesus to heal his servant. Jesus said He was willing to go, but the centurion humbly replied that Jesus only needed to speak a word and his servant would be healed, because he deeply trusted Jesus' authority. Jesus marveled at his faith, and foretold that many would come from all directions to the kingdom of heaven and sit at table with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, while the sons of the kingdom might be thrown into the outer darkness.

This passage reminds us how much Jesus values faith. Both the man with leprosy and the centurion showed faith in Jesus, and so received the grace of a miracle. Through this passage God tells us that faith is the key to meeting Him. When we come before God with faith, He will watch over us, heal us, and give us all that we need.
q: What kind of faith am I showing in my life?
Is my faith strong enough to believe that God can do wonderful things in my life?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for revealing Your great power and love in our lives. Give us faith like the centurion's, believing that Your word can change everything. Help us to keep trusting You and walking with You, until eternity. In the name of Jesus Christ we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: When Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his wife’s mother lying sick with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.
When evening came, they brought to him many possessed with demons. He cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick;
that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “He took our infirmities, and bore our diseases.”
b: This passage describes how Jesus went to Peter's house and found Peter's mother-in-law lying sick with a fever. Jesus touched her hand, the fever left her, and she got up and served Him. That evening, people brought to Jesus many who were demon-possessed, and with a word He drove out the spirits and healed all who were sick. This fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah had said: He took our infirmities and bore our diseases.

Through this passage God tells us that Jesus has authority to heal every kind of sickness, including fever and demon possession. This shows His love and compassion for humanity, and proves that He is the promised Messiah. God's message is that we can trust the power of Jesus; whatever difficulty we face, He can help us through it.
q: Are we willing to entrust our struggles of body, mind and spirit to Jesus? Do we believe He can heal our weakness and sickness?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for Your love and grace, and for showing Your great power in our weakness. Help us to trust in Jesus Christ and find healing and strength in Him. In Jesus' name we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: Now when Jesus saw great multitudes around him, he gave the order to depart to the other side.
A scribe came, and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus said to him, “The foxes have holes, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
Another of his disciples said to him, “Lord, allow me first to go and bury my father.”
But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”
b: This passage tells how, when a crowd was gathered around Him, Jesus gave orders to His disciples to cross to the other side of the lake. A scribe was willing to follow Jesus, but Jesus told him that following Him is not a comfortable thing, for the Son of Man has no place to lay His head. Another disciple wanted to first go and bury his father, but Jesus told him to follow Him at once.

This passage tells us that following Jesus is not smooth sailing. It may mean giving up a comfortable and familiar life, and even facing the opposition of family. Through this passage God reminds us that following Him is a choice; it may bring sacrifice and challenge, but it is the most worthwhile choice of all.
q: Am I willing to let go of comfort and ease to follow Jesus, even if it means facing difficulty and challenge?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for Your guidance and call. Help us to be bold in letting go of everything to follow You, even if it means facing difficulty and challenge. Give us firm faith and courage, that our lives may belong wholly to You. In Jesus' name we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: When he got into a boat, his disciples followed him.
Behold, a violent storm came up on the sea, so much that the boat was covered with the waves, but he was asleep.
They came to him, and woke him up, saying, “Save us, Lord! We are dying!”
He said to them, “Why are you fearful, O you of little faith?”  Then he got up, rebuked the wind and the sea, and there was a great calm.
The men marveled, saying, “What kind of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
b: This passage tells of Jesus and His disciples caught in a storm on the boat. Even though the waves were raging on the sea, Jesus was sleeping peacefully, while the disciples were terrified. When they cried out for help, Jesus rebuked them for their little faith, then got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and the storm became calm.

This passage reminds us that even when we face storms and challenges in life, we should trust in God's power and protection. Jesus' words show us that even in hard times we should not lose faith because of fear, but believe in God's power and promises.
q: How do you respond in the difficult times of your life?
Are you willing to trust God's power and promises?
pr: Dear heavenly Father, thank You for Your presence and protection in our lives. When we face storms and challenges, give us firm faith to believe in Your power and promises. Help us not to be shaken by fear, but to trust wholeheartedly in Your leading and protection. In Jesus' name we pray, amen.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you.

v: When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes,  two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way.
Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?”
Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them.
The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.”
He said to them, “Go!” They came out, and went into the herd of pigs: and behold, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea, and died in the water.
Those who fed them fled, and went away into the city, and told everything, including what happened to those who were possessed with demons.
Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.
b: Matthew 8:28–34

8:28 When he came to the other side, into the country of the Gergesenes,  two people possessed by demons met him there, coming out of the tombs, exceedingly fierce, so that nobody could pass that way. 8:29 Behold, they cried out, saying, “What do we have to do with you, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?” 8:30 Now there was a herd of many pigs feeding far away from them. 8:31 The demons begged him, saying, “If you cast us out, permit us to go away into the herd of pigs.” 8:32 He said to them, “Go!” They came out, and went into the herd of pigs: and behold, the whole herd of pigs rushed down the cliff into the sea, and died in the water. 8:33 Those who fed them fled, and went away into the city, and told everything, including what happened to those who were possessed with demons. 8:34 Behold, all the city came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged that he would depart from their borders.

This passage tells how Jesus met two demon-possessed men in the region of the Gadarenes. They were so fierce that no one dared to pass that way. When they met Jesus, the demons recognized Him as the Son of God and asked whether He had come before the appointed time, hinting at a set time or destiny. The demons begged Jesus not to torment them, but to let them go into a large herd of pigs nearby. Jesus commanded the demons to leave the two men; they went into the pigs, and the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and drowned. When the news spread, the people of the town begged Jesus to leave their region.

This passage emphasizes Jesus' absolute authority over, and control of, the forces of evil. Jesus not only drove out the demons, but the demons themselves acknowledged His divinity and authority. In addition, the passage reflects people's fear and incomprehension of supernatural events, which led them to reject Jesus rather than receive His salvation.

Through this passage God shows us that even when we face extreme evil and distress in life, He is a Savior with power. It encourages us to rely on His strength and sovereignty in every difficulty or fear. It also reminds us that when we face the works of God, our response should be trust and acceptance, not shrinking back out of fear or lack of understanding.
dc: Thank You, Holy Spirit, for guiding us to understand the truth and to walk in it. May God bless you!

v: He entered into a boat, and crossed over, and came into his own city.
Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up! Your sins are forgiven you.”
Behold, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man blasphemes.”
Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil in your hearts?
For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Get up, and walk?’
But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins-” (then he said to the paralytic), “Get up, and take up your mat, and go to your house.”
He arose and departed to his house.
But when the multitudes saw it, they marveled and glorified God, who had given such authority to men.
b: Matthew 9:1–8.

9:1 He entered into a boat, and crossed over, and came into his own city. 9:2 Behold, they brought to him a man who was paralyzed, lying on a bed. Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, cheer up!
